Convert Wide Method Comparison Data to Long Format

Source: R/mc_long.R
mc_long.Rd

Converts data with one column per measurement method into the long format (one row per measurement) used by method_vc() and sim_methods().

Usage

mc_long(
  data,
  methods,
  id = NULL,
  replicate = NULL,
  names_to = "method",
  values_to = "y"
)

Arguments

data

A data frame in wide format, with one column per method.

methods

Character vector naming the method columns (at least two). The order sets the order of the method factor levels; the first is the reference method.

id

Name of the column identifying the item (subject). If NULL (default), each row is treated as a separate item and an id column is created from the row number.

replicate

Name of the column identifying the replicate (measurement occasion). If NULL and some items have more than one row, a replicate column is created from the row order within each item (with a message): methods recorded on the same row are then treated as measured on the same occasion.

names_to

Name of the new column holding the method names. Default is "method".

values_to

Name of the new column holding the measurements. Default is "y".

Value

A tibble with columns for the item identifier (named as in id, or id if created), the replicate (if supplied or created), the method (a factor with levels in the order of methods), and the measurement. Rows with a missing measurement are kept.

See also

method_vc(), sim_methods()

Examples

data("reps")
# reps has replicate pairs of x and y measured on the same occasion
reps_long = mc_long(reps, methods = c("x", "y"), id = "id")
#> Some items have several rows; a 'replicate' column was created from the row order within each item.
head(reps_long)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#>      id replicate method     y
#>   <int>     <int> <fct>  <dbl>
#> 1     1         1 x       7.83
#> 2     1         1 y       6.57
#> 3     1         2 x       7.42
#> 4     1         2 y       5.62
#> 5     1         3 x       7.89
#> 6     1         3 y       6.9
